chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from a slave whom Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) emancipated —

'This is what Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both) emancipated: he emancipated his Sindhi slave, so-and-so, upon the condition that he would testify that there is no deity except Allah, alone, with no partner for Him; and that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger; and that the Resurrection is true; and that Paradise is true; and that the Fire is true;

and upon the condition that he would befriend the friends of Allah, and would disavow from the enemies of Allah, and would permit what Allah has permitted, and would forbid what Allah has forbidden, and would believe in the Messengers of Allah, and would acknowledge what came from the presence of Allah. I emancipate him for the Face of Allah, not seeking by it any recompense nor gratitude, and no one has any claim over him except in goodness.' Witnessed by so-and-so.

key_terms.الْبَعْثُ: the Resurrection, literally 'the sending forth' — belief in bodily resurrection on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.تَبَرَّأَ: to disavow, to declare oneself free from — the Shia concept of tabarra, dissociation from enemies of Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.سَبِيلٌ: a way, a path — in legal context, a claim or authority over a person
key_terms.لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ: for the Face of Allah — a classical formula indicating an act done purely for God's sake without worldly reward
key_terms.وَالَى: to befriend, to take as ally — the Shia concept of tawalla, loyalty to the Imams and their followers

ai.seo_question: What conditions did Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq place on the emancipation of his slave according to Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith preserves the actual manumission deed of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS), in which he emancipated his Sindhi slave on the condition of affirming core Islamic beliefs and Shia loyalties. The document encapsulates the Shia creedal formula: tawhid (divine unity), prophethood of Muhammad (SAWA), resurrection, and tawalla/tabarra (loyalty to Allah's friends, disavowal of His enemies). Historically, such conditional emancipations were legally recognized in classical Islamic jurisprudence, and this particular document is significant as it links manumission directly to religious commitment — freedom as inseparable from faith.
